samples.summary: The new "one line per error, with `command`" stderr invariant is broken by the sibling error paths that bypass `outputError`
samples.evidence: `outputError` now emits a single-line envelope with `command` (formatter.ts:83-91) and the tests assert `expect(raw).not.toContain('\n')`. But several real error paths never go through `outputError` and still emit pretty-printed, multi-line JSON with no `command` field: docs.ts:195 and docs.ts:255 (backend-shaped error on `docs content` / `docs export`, e.g. TYPE_MISMATCH), notes.ts:148 and notes.ts:203, slides.ts:154 and slides.ts:204, schema.ts:32 (`Unknown command`), plus the import/upload helpers (docs/import.ts:164,194,201,211,245; notes/import.ts:159,188,197,212; slides/import.ts:194,237,244,254,312; files/upload.ts:217,227; files/download.ts:57) which all use `JSON.stringify(..., null, 2)`. A caller that follows the newly documented contract and reads stderr with a line-delimited parser will fail on these — the very paths the change claims to make attributable. Nothing in the change guards or migrates them.

samples.summary: `runCli` mutates the caller-supplied program by registering a `preAction` hook on every call, so repeated calls accumulate hooks
samples.evidence: `program.hook('preAction', ...)` is registered inside `runCli` on the (possibly caller-owned, possibly already-parsed) `program`. Commander appends to `_lifeCycleHooks`, it does not replace, so calling `runCli(sameProgram, ...)` twice registers the closure twice and each subsequent invocation adds another. Behaviour is currently benign (both closures assign the same value to different `acting` bindings) and `bin.ts` calls it once, but the side effect on an argument is a latent leak: the older closures and their captured programs stay reachable from the program for the process lifetime, and any future non-idempotent hook body would run N times.

samples.summary: `acting` is never cleared, so the last-resort envelope can attribute an error to a command that already finished
samples.evidence: The `preAction` hook only sets `acting`; nothing resets it after the action resolves. Any throw that escapes `parseAsync` after the action completed — e.g. from a `postAction` hook, from commander's own post-action bookkeeping, or from code in a chained `parseAsync` continuation — is attributed to the last command that started, which may not be the failing site. The field is documented as "omitted rather than guessed when no command is known", but in this window it is guessed rather than omitted.

verdict.reason: Every claimed location checks out. outputError (formatter.ts:80-93) emits a single-line envelope and its own comment (formatter.ts:69-73) asserts "one line per error ... line-delimited parser"; docs/design/cli.md:1017-1018 and packages/cli/README.md:116-118 document that contract. Yet docs.ts:195 and docs.ts:255 forward the backend body via console.error(JSON.stringify(body, null, 2)) and return before outputError (docs.ts:213), producing multi-line JSON with no `command`. The same pattern exists at notes.ts:148,203, slides.ts:154,204, and the import/upload helpers (docs/import.ts:164,194,211; notes/import.ts:159,188,212; slides/import.ts:194,237,254; files/upload.ts:217,227; files/download.ts:57). This is reachable on a flagship documented case: cli.md:1028 lists `docs.content` on a sheet document -> TYPE_MISMATCH, which is exactly the body forwarded at docs.ts:195. So the invariant the change introduces and tests is violated on real error paths — a broken invariant / wrong observable behavior, in the Correctness lane. The task todo (20260811-...-todo.md:19-22) declares these emitters out of scope for #654/#655, but per instructions I must not judge whether the change introduced the code, only whether the defect is real and reachable — and it is. No guard elsewhere normalizes these emissions.
